item.title: Do Teachers Have Free Speech? CT Panel Grapples With The Issue At Education Summit
item.description: State Sen. John Kissel, R-Enfield, said teachers shouldn’t have to choose between basic American freedoms and their career.

item.title: Today’s Toons
item.description: Editorial cartoons by RJ Matson & Jonathan Brown

item.title: DOT Reports Traffic Fatalities Declined In 2025, But Bicycle And Pedestrian Deaths Rose
item.description: Despite the overall drop in fatalities, pedestrian and bicyclist deaths increased with speeding the leading factor in serious crashes, according to the department’s data.

item.title: Hartford Vigil For Alex Pretti Set For Saturday
item.description: CT Nurses United is organizing a vigil Saturday outside the Capitol to honor and remember an ICU nurse killed in Minneapolis last weekend.

item.title: CT Joins 21 States Denouncing Justice Dept. ‘Occupation’ Of Minnesota
item.description: In a letter to U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi and Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem, the coalition condemned the Trump administration’s effort to exploit the situation in Minnesota to pressure state leaders into turning over sensitive resident data and dismantling longstanding public safety policies.

item.title: Youth Social Media Use Would Get Parent-Controlled Defaults, Mandatory Reporting Under Proposed CT Legislation
item.description: Similar legislation passed the state House of Representatives 121-26 last year, but the session ended without a vote in the Senate.

item.title: CT Draws $18.7M From Emergency Fund To Offset Federal Funding Cuts
item.description: Connecticut officials announced a second draw from the state’s $500 million Emergency State Response Reserve on Thursday, committing $18.7 million to offset federal funding cuts and administrative disruptions that state leaders said are threatening food assistance, health coverage, mental health services, and school-based support programs.

item.title: Connecticut Shoreline Residents Revisit Intense Storms As They Ready For More
item.description: Complications faced by Connecticut shoreline residents during tropical storms and hurricanes in the last 15 years demonstrate an increased intensity in storms affecting the Northeast region of the United States as climate change continues.

item.title: CT Health Commissioner Backs Pediatric Group’s Vaccine Recommendations Over CDC’s
item.description: Connecticut, and 14 other states in the Governors Public Health Alliance, have elected not to adopt changes to the vaccine schedule proposed by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

item.title: Health Care Workers Hold Vigil At CT Capitol For ICU Nurse Killed By Federal Agents In Minneapolis
item.description: Speakers at the Hartford vigil repeatedly linked Pretti’s death to immigration enforcement activity they said is already being felt in Connecticut, citing detentions in communities including Newington and Southington.
